transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess… things with my wife have been bothering me. Her late meetings, small changes in her work messages—she says it’s all normal office stuff, but it’s been going on long enough that it doesn’t feel random to me. Like there’s some kind of private signal in it, something she’s not saying directly.
Do you feel certain that your wife is sending hidden messages, or is it something you think might be true?

I… I’d say I’m pretty sure. She says it’s just normal office stuff, but the late meetings and those small changes in her messages have been lining up too precisely for about a year. It doesn’t feel accidental to me. It feels like there’s something in it she’s trying to tell me without saying it straight out.
If your wife showed you clear proof that there were no hidden messages, would you believe her?
I’d look at it, sure. But… I don’t know. It’s hard to just ignore how it’s all lined up for so long. If it was really clear, maybe, but I’d still wonder what I was missing.
Do you ever feel that other people besides your wife are sending you hidden messages?
No… not really other people. It’s mainly my wife. The late meetings and the little changes in her work messages… they’ve just lined up too much over the past year to feel random.
Do you believe your wife is being unfaithful to you?
I… I don’t like saying it that way. I just know the late meetings and the changes in her messages don’t feel accidental. It feels like she’s signaling something she won’t say directly.
Has your wife directly told you that there are no hidden messages in what she says or writes?

Yes. She’s said that… that it’s just normal office stuff, the late meetings and the wording in her messages. But it’s been going on so long, and it lines up too neatly. I can’t just believe it’s accidental.
Has anyone shown you clear evidence that your wife is not sending hidden messages?
Not clear evidence, no. She says it’s normal office stuff, and maybe other people would see it that way, but… over the past year it’s lined up too precisely for me to think it’s just accidental.
Have you checked your wife’s phone, email, or messages to look for proof?

I’d rather not get into her phone or email. It’s more… the late meetings, the small changes in her work messages. She says it’s normal office stuff, but after a year it just lines up too neatly, like there’s some private signal there.
Do you ever think you might be mistaken about your wife sending hidden messages?

I’ve wondered that, yes… but I don’t think so. I know she says it’s just normal office things, the late meetings and wording changes, but it’s been about a year and it lines up too precisely. It doesn’t feel accidental to me.
Has this situation with your wife caused problems for you at work or in other parts of your life?

Mostly at home. It’s caused some tense conversations with my wife… enough that the couples therapist said maybe I should talk to someone on my own. Work’s been okay, though. I still keep up with my usual routines and everything.
Do you think your wife is deliberately trying to deceive or harm you?

Harm me? No, I wouldn’t put it that way. Deceive… maybe. I just think there’s something in those late meetings and the way her work messages change. It’s gone on long enough that it feels deliberate, like she’s trying to tell me something without saying it directly.
Have you generally found it hard to trust other people, even before these concerns about your wife began?
I don’t know… I wouldn’t say it was a general problem. I mean, I’ve never been the most open person, but this feels more specific than that.
If your wife sat down with you and explained each late meeting and message change in a way that made sense, would you accept that there were no hidden signals?

I’d listen, sure. But… I don’t know if an explanation would cover all of it. The meetings and the little changes in her messages have lined up too neatly for too long. It just doesn’t feel like normal office stuff to me.
Aside from concerns about your wife, do you spend a lot of time worrying about many other things in your life?
Not really. I mean… I have normal things on my mind, work, bills, that kind of thing, but I wouldn’t say I spend a lot of time worrying about everything.
Do you believe your wife is having an affair?

I… I think something is going on, yes. She says the late meetings and the changes in her work messages are just normal office things, but over the past year they’ve lined up too exactly. It feels like there’s some kind of private signal there… something she isn’t saying to me directly.
If you were shown definite proof that your wife was not having an affair, would you still believe that something was going on?

I guess… if it was really definite proof, I’d have to think about it. But I don’t think it would make all of it disappear for me. The late meetings, the small message changes… they’ve lined up too precisely for too long. It still feels like some kind of private signal, even if she says it’s just work.
Has anyone shown you direct proof that your wife was faithful?
No… not direct proof, I guess. She says it’s just work—late meetings, messages changing a little—but it’s been going on so long and it lines up too neatly. It doesn’t feel accidental to me.
If you saw clear proof that your wife was not having an affair, would you still believe she was sending you hidden signals?

I… maybe. If it was clear proof, I’d try to accept that part. But the meetings and those little changes in her work messages… they’ve lined up for so long, too neatly. It still feels like there’s some kind of signal there, something she won’t just say.
Have you ever heard voices when no one was there?
No… I don’t think so. I haven’t heard voices when nobody was there.
Did this belief about your wife start suddenly?
Not all at once, no. It’s been… about a year, I suppose. Since she started working outside the home again.
